capabilities: Convert selected or pasted text into a fenced code block
Choose which candidate languages are considered in settings
Fall back to an unlabelled block for ambiguous or plain-prose input
extras: README states detection limitations: HTML is labeled xml, TOML uses the ini grammar, and C vs C++ cannot always be distinguished; wrong labels can be fixed by editing the fence or narrowing enabled languages.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to turn text into a code block or guess the language, so users must add fences and language labels manually.
summary: Code block converter that wraps selected or pasted text in a fenced code block with automatic programming language detection.
